content: ICD-10 Chapter I focuses on certain infectious and parasitic diseases, which are generally recognized as communicable or transmissible. For cases where drug resistance is associated with the disease, an additional code (Z16) should be used to specify this resistance. The chapter excludes certain conditions, such as individuals who are carriers or suspected carriers of infectious diseases (Z22), localized infections, infectious and parasitic diseases that complicate pregnancy, childbirth, and the puerperium (O98), as well as influenza and other acute respiratory infections (J00-J22). Additionally, it excludes infectious and parasitic diseases specific to the perinatal period (P35-P39). The chapter is divided into the following categories: A00-A09: Intestinal infectious diseases, which include conditions such as cholera, typhoid, and other diarrheal diseases. A15-A19: Tuberculosis, encompassing all forms of the disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. A20-A28: Certain zoonotic bacterial diseases, which are infections transmitted from animals to humans, such as plague and anthrax. A30-A49: Other bacterial diseases, including leprosy and diphtheria. A50-A64: Infections that are predominantly transmitted through sexual contact, such as syphilis and gonorrhea. A65-A69: Other spirochetal diseases, including conditions like Lyme disease and relapsing fever. A70-A74: Diseases caused by chlamydiae, such as trachoma and psittacosis. A75-A79: Rickettsioses, which are infections caused by Rickettsia species, such as typhus and Rocky Mountain spotted fever. A80-A89: Viral infections of the central nervous system, including poliomyelitis and viral encephalitis. A90-A99: Arthropod-borne viral fevers and viral hemorrhagic fevers, such as dengue fever and Ebola virus disease. B00-B09: Viral infections characterized by lesions on the skin and mucous membranes, such as herpes simplex and varicella (chickenpox). B10: Other human herpesvirus infections not classified elsewhere. B15-B19: Viral hepatitis, including hepatitis A, B, C, D, and E. B20: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease, encompassing all stages of HIV infection. B25-B34: Other viral diseases, such as mumps, measles, and rubella. B35-B49: Mycoses, which are fungal infections like candidiasis and aspergillosis. B50-B64: Protozoal diseases, including malaria and toxoplasmosis. B65-B83: Helminthiases, which are parasitic worm infections such as schistosomiasis and ascariasis. B85-B89: Infestations caused by organisms like lice (pediculosis) and mites (acariasis). B90-B94: Sequelae of infectious and parasitic diseases, referring to long-term complications or conditions resulting from these infections. B95-B97: Codes for identifying bacterial, viral, and other infectious agents that are the cause of diseases classified elsewhere. B99: Other infectious diseases that do not fall into the above categories.
